title: OSPF with two areas
summary: Split an OSPF network into a backbone and a second area joined by a border router, then reach one LAN from the other.
objectives: Place links in the backbone (area 0) and in a second area
Make the middle router an area border router by giving it a link in each area
Learn routes across the area boundary and ping end to end

tasks.title: Start OSPF with unique router IDs
tasks.description: Start OSPF process 1 on all three routers with router IDs 1.1.1.1 (R1), 2.2.2.2 (R2) and 3.3.3.3 (R3).
hints: Two routers with the same router ID will not become neighbours.
Example on R1: system-view, then ospf 1 router-id 1.1.1.1

tasks.title: Build the backbone (area 0)
tasks.description: The link between R1 and R2 (198.51.100.0/30) and the R1 LAN (192.0.2.0/25) belong to area 0. Advertise them on R1, and the link on R2.
hints: Both ends of a link must put it in the same area, or the routers will not become neighbours.
A network statement ends with a wildcard mask: 0.0.0.3 for a /30, 0.0.0.127 for a /25.
Example on R1: ospf 1 area 0 network 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.3 and ospf 1 area 0 network 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.127. On R2: ospf 1 area 0 network 198.51.100.0 0.0.0.3

criteria.label: R1 and R2 are OSPF neighbours

tasks.title: Add area 1 behind the border router
tasks.description: The link between R2 and R3 (198.51.100.4/30) and the R3 LAN (203.0.113.0/25) belong to area 1. R2 now has one link in area 0 and one in area 1: it is the area border router.
hints: Use area 1 in the network statements for 198.51.100.4/30 on both R2 and R3.
Example on R2: ospf 1 area 1 network 198.51.100.4 0.0.0.3. On R3: ospf 1 area 1 network 198.51.100.4 0.0.0.3 and ospf 1 area 1 network 203.0.113.0 0.0.0.127

criteria.label: R2 and R3 are OSPF neighbours

tasks.title: Learn routes across the areas
tasks.description: Routes from area 1 must reach the backbone and the other way round: R1 learns the area 1 networks and R3 learns the area 0 networks.
hints: Areas that do not touch area 0 do not exchange routes. Check that the link to R1 is in area 0 on both routers.
If a LAN is missing, its network statement is probably missing on the router that owns it.

tasks.title: Ping from LAN to LAN
tasks.description: OSPF routes are now used for forwarding. PC1 and PC3 must reach each other.
hints: Both directions must work: the reply needs a route back too.
